safety.crash: If the engine crashes, traffic may go direct. This is not a protected mode.
set.autostart.text: Via the task scheduler, with admin rights and no extra prompt. The window doesn't open, Waarp stays in the tray.
set.auto.text: Enable routes right after the app starts.
set.tray.text: The close button hides the window, routes keep working.
set.notify.down: Server went down or came back

set.ru.text: When on, .ru, .рф, banks and Gosuslugi go direct from any app, even if that app is set to use a tunnel.
set.dns.text: More reliable against address spoofing by the ISP, but Russian sites may open a bit slower.
set.lan.text: Printers, NAS, the router and other local devices stay reachable outside the tunnel. Turn off if private addresses should follow Waarp's rules.
set.reset.text: Closes tunnels and kills a stuck engine. Doesn't touch other VPNs or Windows settings.
set.reset.error: Couldn't fully close the Waarp processes
set.log.text: Last lines, keys are masked. Useful if something isn't working.
set.how.1: Waarp brings up its own adapter and decides for each connection where to send it: direct or through one of your servers. It decides by app, domain or IP.
set.how.2: A site rule beats an app rule. If YouTube goes through Server 1, it will go through it even from a browser that is set to direct.
set.how.3: While Waarp is running, if a server is unavailable, its apps wait for recovery and don't switch to direct. If the engine crashes, protection is not guaranteed yet.
set.how.4: Waarp doesn't touch AmneziaVPN and other VPNs. If a tunnel address matches or a full route conflicts, Waarp will warn you and won't start a second system tunnel.
set.how.5: Keys are stored encrypted via Windows (DPAPI) and don't show up in the log.

wel.title: Hi. Let's set up Waarp
wel.text: Your own routes through your AmneziaWG and VLESS servers, like ExitLag, but for anything. Each app and site gets its own path: direct, through Server 1 or through Server 2.
wel.1: In your server panel (wg-easy or AmneziaVPN) create a new profile, for example “PC-waarp”. One config won't work for two apps at once.
wel.2: Waarp will take a link or config from the clipboard, or open a file. You can add as many servers as you want.
wel.3: in “Cards”, pick a tunnel for each and flip the switch at the top.

diag.engine.on.hint: A specific address is checked below. A running process alone does not confirm access to the site.
diag.engine.off.hint: The check will compare the system path with the available connections, without turning on the VPN for the whole computer.
diag.engine.changing.hint: We will wait for the switch to finish and check the new path.

diag.reason.main_down: The main path is not responding; currently using {v}.
diag.reason.path_down: Connection {v} did not respond in two consecutive rounds. Below you can compare this address with another path.
diag.reason.engine_down: The local core is not responding. First restore its startup on Home.
diag.reason.missing: The selected connection was removed or is unavailable. Choose an existing one in the route card.
diag.reason.busy: The connection key is already in use. Free it on another device or choose another connection.
diag.reason.waiting: The path has not been confirmed as working yet. An unchecked path is not considered broken.
diag.more.issues: More routes with issues: {n}. They are shown on Home.
diag.extra: Additional checks: data transfer and response history
diag.extra.hint: Use them when the address responds but you need to separately check data loading or how the response time changes.
diag.stages: Check stages over the system path
diag.result.dns-system: System DNS did not find the address
diag.detail.dns-system: DNS over HTTPS got the address, but system DNS did not. This is a specific difference between the two ways of resolving the name.
diag.next.dns-system: If there is a confirmed working path below, use it for this address. Otherwise check the DNS settings of the active network connection and run the check again.
diag.result.dns-missing: Both DNS did not find this domain
diag.detail.dns-missing: The system and DNS over HTTPS both returned “name not found”. The system TCP connection was not checked after that.
diag.next.dns-missing: Check the spelling of the domain and paste the full address from the browser. If the address is correct, compare with another site: it is too early to change the VPN server.
diag.result.dns-unreachable: Could not get the server address
diag.detail.dns-unreachable: The name check did not complete successfully either through the system or through DNS over HTTPS. This does not prove the server itself is unreachable.
diag.next.dns-unreachable: Check whether another site opens. On a public Wi-Fi network, first go through its sign-in page, then run the check for the needed address again.
diag.result.network-unreachable: No network route to the address
diag.detail.network-unreachable: The system reported that the network or host is unreachable, before the TCP connection was established.
diag.next.network-unreachable: Check the active Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection. If the network has just changed, wait until it gets an address and run the check again.
diag.detail.tcp-refused: The address was found, but the connection over the system path is interrupted before TLS and the site's response. A single reset cannot tell who caused it.
diag.next.tcp-refused: Compare the connection results below. If one of them responded twice, you can route this address through it; if not, check another address to separate a general failure from a problem with this site.
diag.result.tcp-timeout: The server did not respond to the TCP connection
diag.detail.tcp-timeout: DNS worked, but the connection was not established within the check time. A timeout does not show where exactly the response was lost.
diag.next.tcp-timeout: Compare this same address through the connections below. No response on only one path shows which path is worth replacing; no response on all of them means checking another site.
diag.detail.tcp-failed: The server name was resolved, but the TCP connection ended with an error. TLS and HTTP were not checked after that.
diag.next.tcp-failed: Compare the connection results below. If none responded, check another site and the network state before changing routes.
diag.detail.tls-certificate: The TCP connection was established, but the TLS certificate received does not meet the verification requirements.
diag.next.tls-certificate: Check the Windows date and time and that the domain is correct. Do not turn off certificate checks: if the problem remains only with this site, its certificate needs to be fixed.
diag.detail.tls-failed: The address was found and TCP works, but the TLS handshake of the system request did not complete. HTTP was not checked after that.
diag.next.tls-failed: Check the result through another path below. If the address responds through it, use the confirmed option; the reason for the TLS break over the system path is not known yet.
diag.result.http-method: The site does not accept the test request
diag.detail.http-method: The connection was established, but the site rejected both forms of the test HTTP request. This result does not mean the site does not work in a browser.
diag.next.http-method: Open the full address in a browser. For automatic comparison, use another page of this service that is available without signing in.
diag.result.http-redirect: The site responded with a redirect
diag.detail.http-redirect: Got HTTP {n}. Next address: {to}. This check did not follow it.
diag.next.http-redirect: If the redirect leads to a sign-in page, sign in in the browser. To check the final page, paste its full address in the field above.
diag.result.http-denied: The site responds but restricts the request
diag.detail.http-denied: Got HTTP {n}. The network connection reached the server's response; the refusal may depend on sign-in, site rules or request rate.
diag.next.http-denied: Check the same address in a browser and sign in to your account if the site requires it. With code 429, wait for the limit to end. Changing the path only makes sense if the responses are confirmed to differ.
diag.result.http-server: The site returned a server error
diag.detail.http-server: Got HTTP {n}. The request reached the HTTP server, which reported a processing error.
diag.next.http-server: Compare the response through another path below. If the error repeats, try another page of this service or wait for it to be fixed on its side.
diag.detail.http-status: The connection was established, but the server rejected this HTTP request. The response code is shown in the results.
diag.next.http-status: Check the full page address, that the page exists and whether sign-in is needed. If the page you need opens in a browser, this test request is not suitable for judging the whole service.
diag.result.http-ok: The address responded over the system path
diag.detail.http-ok: Establishing the connection and the test HTTP request both completed successfully. This confirms the address responds, but not that all app functions work.
diag.next.http-ok: If the problem remains in the app, check the address where the error occurs, not just the home page. For stalling downloads, open the additional data transfer check below.
diag.result.http-timeout: Connected, but the site's response did not arrive in time
diag.detail.http-timeout: DNS and connection setup passed, but the HTTP response did not arrive within the check time.
diag.next.http-timeout: Compare the time and number of responses through the connections below. If only one page is slow, check another page of the same service.
diag.result.http-failed: The request broke off before an HTTP response
diag.detail.http-failed: The earlier connection stages completed, but the test request did not get an HTTP response.
diag.next.http-failed: Paste the full address of the problem page and compare the responses of the paths below. If they respond, check how this address works in the app itself.
diag.result.incomplete: The check could not be completed
diag.detail.incomplete: Not enough results to point to the stage of the network failure. A skipped stage is not counted as an error.
diag.next.incomplete: Wait for the network or connection change to finish and run the check again. The current core state is shown above the results.
diag.current.responded: Through {v} got {n} of {total} responses. This is a check of the selected connection; the system request below is checked separately.
diag.next.keep: The current path got a response, so there is no need to change it based on this result. If the app still doesn't work, check the address where it stops, or open the data transfer check below.
diag.stages.hint: Request sent through Windows network routes. App traffic may take a different path.
